prompt:
Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

## Review Feedback


## Inline Code Comments
[0] images/keystone/Dockerfile:44: `apt-get install` fails with default empty `EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES`

When the image is built locally without explicitly passing `--build-arg EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES=...`, the `ARG` default of `""` means `${EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES}` expands to nothing. On Ubuntu Noble (apt 2.7.x), `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends` with no package arguments exits with a non-zero code (`E: No packages specified`), failing the build with a cryptic error rather than a helpful message.

While the CI workflow always provides packages (enforced by the empty-check in `Resolve extra packages`), a developer following the local build instructions who omits `--build-arg EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES=...` gets a confusing failure. A conditional guard would make this more resilient:

```suggestion
RUN if [ -n "${EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES}" ]; then \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ${EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES} && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    fi
```

Alternatively, a comment noting that this ARG must be non-empty (or that `docs/reference/container-images.md` step 3 shows the required `--build-arg`) would also help.
